# Proverbs 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD despises dishonest scales, but accurate weights make Him glad.

**2** When pride arrives, humiliation follows — but wisdom is found with the humble.

**3** Integrity guides honest people, but duplicity destroys the dishonest.

**4** Money won't help you on judgment day, but living right can save your life.

**5** A good person's integrity clears the road ahead, but a wicked person trips over their own sin.

**6** Doing right rescues honest people, but the treacherous are trapped by their own cravings.

**7** When a wicked person dies, their hope dies with them — everything they counted on disappears.

**8** The righteous person escapes trouble, and it falls on the wicked instead.

**9** A godless person can ruin their neighbor just by talking, but knowledge protects the righteous.

**10** When good people succeed, the whole city celebrates. When the wicked fall, people cheer.

**11** A city rises when upright people speak blessings, but wicked people's words tear it down.

**12** Putting down your neighbor shows you have no sense. A smart person keeps their mouth shut.

**13** A gossip can't keep a secret, but a trustworthy person protects what's been shared in confidence.

**14** Without wise leadership, a nation collapses — but with many advisors, there is safety.

**15** Co-signing a loan for a stranger is asking for trouble. Refusing to pledge is the safe move.

**16** A gracious woman earns respect, just as aggressive men seize wealth.

**17** Being kind to others is actually being kind to yourself. Being cruel only damages you.

**18** The wicked earn paychecks that don't last, but those who plant righteousness harvest a real reward.

**19** Genuine righteousness leads to life, but chasing evil leads to death.

**20** The LORD can't stand people with twisted hearts, but He delights in those who walk a straight path.

**21** Make no mistake — the guilty will be punished. But the children of the righteous will be safe.

**22** A beautiful woman who lacks good judgment is like a gold ring stuck in a pig's nose.

**23** What the righteous hope for always turns out good; what the wicked expect ends in fury.

**24** Some people give generously and end up with more. Others hold on too tightly and wind up with less.

**25** A generous person will prosper. Refresh others, and you yourself will be refreshed.

**26** People curse the one who hoards grain, but they bless the person willing to sell.

**27** If you pursue good things, you'll earn favor. If you go looking for trouble, trouble will find you.

**28** Anyone who trusts in their money will eventually fall, but the righteous flourish like green leaves.

**29** Bring trouble to your own family and you'll inherit nothing but wind. A fool ends up working for the wise.

**30** The righteous produce fruit that sustains life. A person who wins hearts is truly wise.

**31** If even the righteous get what's coming to them on earth, imagine what awaits the wicked and the sinner!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **11:2**: Short, sharp, unforgettable. The moment pride walks in the door, humiliation is right behind it.

- **11:22**: Possibly the funniest image in the entire Bible — a gold ring in a pig's snout. It's meant to be absurd, and that's the point.

- **11:24-25**: The generosity paradox — one of the deepest truths in Proverbs. The tighter you grip, the less you have. Open your hands, and more comes back.

— PNEUMA
